newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-OPEN PRACTICE BEGINS FOR INDY 500.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-OPEN PRACTICE BEGINS FOR INDY 500.

text.p: Veteran drivers will take the track as open practice for all drivers begins on Tuesday for the Indianapolis 500 at Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

United States Auto Club (USAC) chief steward Keith Ward said that rookie training would continue daily as needed in the morning hours to allow drivers a chance to complete the first four phases of the five-phase USAC test for the race.

"We'll do it on a day-by-day basis as necessary," Ward said, adding that the fifth phase of the test, which requires 10 laps turned at over 200 miles per hour (320 kph) with observation by veteran drivers, will be done during regular hours.
"That's so the veteran drivers at their posts get the opportunity to see them run in traffic a little bit."
Kenny Brack of Sweden and Vincenzo Sospiri of Italy have completed the first four phases of the test. Lap speeds are gradually increased during the training stages.

Among the drivers who could begin practicing Tuesday are defending champion Buddy Lazier, 1990 champion Arie Luyendyk, rising star Tony Stewart, two-time runner-up Scott Goodyear and Gary Bettenhausen, a 55-year-old veteran of 21 Indy 500 starts.
Pole qualifying for the 81st Indy 500 is set for this Saturday. The race is scheduled for 200 laps around the 2.5-mile (4 km) oval on May 25.
